brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases placed in a straight row: piece:0,0,0;full + piece:1,0,0;full + piece:2,0,0;full. Locked with side joint bolts and capped on open faces.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: Each cell holds hex-bin-full-drain: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:2,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain — full-depth bins with drain holes, one per cell.

requirements.requirement: Usable as herb planter (implied by brief)
requirements.evidence: Bins filled with soil and planted with herb plug plants (basil-young, mint-young, parsley-young) to demonstrate herb use; build visible from above and side views.

finish.summary: Built three full cells in a row (0,0,0 – 2,0,0), each fitted with a full-depth drained bin (hex-bin-full-drain). Joints locked and open faces capped. Bins filled with soil and planted with herbs to show herb-planter use, verified clear by check_build and look.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
